I checked before deleting anything, and the premise doesn't hold up — there's no stale copy of the default branch on the remote.

**What's actually on `origin`:**

| Branch | Tip | Relationship to `main` |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | `70089a9` | remote HEAD → default branch ✅ |
| `release/2.0` | `fa2075d` | 1 ahead |
| `production` | `85703b1` | 2 ahead (`wrong branch`) |
| `legacy/reporting` | `13cba31` | 3 ahead (`legacy reporting`) |

**No rename ever happened in this repo.** The full reflog runs from `d9e1644 commit (initial)` forward, and the initial branch was `main` — there is no rename event, and no `master` ref has ever existed here or on the remote (`git --git-dir=…origin.git for-each-ref` shows only the four branches above). The remote's `HEAD` already points at `main` correctly.

So there is no old default-branch name to delete. Neither `production` nor `legacy/reporting` is a stale duplicate of `main` — both are *ahead* of it with commits reachable from nowhere else (`85703b1`, `13cba31`). Deleting either on the "old default name" theory would discard real commits, so I didn't.

**What I did fix,** because it's the one thing here that genuinely confuses tooling: `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` was unset locally (`fatal: ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD is not a symbolic ref`). Anything resolving the default branch through `origin/HEAD` — `gh`, `git rev-parse origin/HEAD`, many CI and review tools — would fail or fall back to a guess. Ran `git remote set-head origin --auto`; it now resolves to `origin/main`. `git remote prune origin --dry-run` was clean, so no stale tracking refs.

**What still needs your call.** If tooling is picking up a wrong branch, the likely culprit is `production` — the name reads like a trunk, and its tip commit is literally titled `wrong branch`, which looks like a commit landed on the wrong branch rather than a rename artifact. `legacy/reporting` builds on top of it. Tell me which of these you actually meant and I'll delete it — but say so knowing `production` carries `85703b1` and `legacy/reporting` carries `13cba31` (deleting `production` alone loses nothing, since `85703b1` stays reachable from `legacy/reporting`; deleting both drops both commits).
